BaseId.description: Identifies a warm base: the substrate a unit's home is cloned from.

CommitId.description: A Git object id in full, lowercase hexadecimal form.

Digest.description:
A content digest, lowercase hex. The algorithm is the fingerprint module's
choice; the model only fixes the form.

Platform.description:
A target triple, for example `aarch64-apple-darwin`. Part of the workspace
fingerprint, because a base built on one platform is not warm on another.

ProjectId.description: Identifies a project: one Git repository Nodal manages units for.

Provenance.description:
What built a base, and with what.

A base is minutes of work that a later release may no longer produce the same way,
and until this record existed a base could not say which release made it, which
commands it ran or which tools answered them. A person looking at a base that
behaves unlike a fresh one had nothing to compare.

It is not part of the key. A base is keyed by its workspace fingerprint and its
platform, and none of this changes that: a base built by an older Nodal is still
warm, and this is what makes that visible rather than making it cold.

install.description: Every install it ran, in order, each as the argument list it was given.

recipe.description: The effective recipe the build read, by content.

tools.description:
What each tool answered when it was asked its version, by the name the recipe
records that tool under.

warm.description: The build it ran afterwards, empty when it was not asked for one.

Timestamp.description: A UTC instant, serialised as an RFC 3339 string.

ToolVersion.description: The version a toolchain pins a tool to, as written in the pin file.

Version.description:
A program's version: dot-separated numbers, with a pre-release or a build after
them, as the program writes it.

WorkspaceFp.description: The key a warm base is stored under.

description:
One base: a clean checkout with dependencies installed, keyed by the workspace
fingerprint it was built for. A unit's home is a copy-on-write clone of one of these.

commit.description: The commit the base was built at.

last_used.description: Last time a unit was materialised from it; the input to eviction.

path.description: Where the base lives on this host.

platform.description: The target triple it was built on; a base is not warm on another platform.

project_id.description: The project this base belongs to.

provenance.description:
What built it. `None` for a base built before a base recorded this, which is
the one thing a stale base cannot be asked about.

ws_fingerprint.description: The workspace fingerprint this base is warm for.

title: Base
